advances: Intrinsic Hausdorff-measure transport capacities on a mixed trace, including degenerate traces. These are not halfspace-depth constants.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
An integer midpoint forces both endpoint bases to have the same parity, so the old coupling splits into classwise couplings with equal marginal masses. Work in a nonzero class. Its support product is compact, and every product midpoint belongs to $S$ by parity and convexity. The continuous function $H_q$ is nondecreasing in each argument, including at zeros, so its composite with the two bounded upper semicontinuous ceilings is upper semicontinuous. Each nonempty compact midpoint preimage attains its maximum. A sequence of maximizing pairs for convergent outputs has a convergent subsequence when the limsup of the envelopes is positive. Upper semicontinuity of the composite then bounds this limsup by the value at the limiting midpoint. This proves the asserted regularity, including at outputs outside the compact midpoint set.

For $q>0$ use the common fiber direction $L$ from the intrinsic parity direction lemma. Identify the physical coordinates isometrically with the auxiliary base $(z,b)$ and the $q$ coordinates along $L$. Each endpoint fiber lies above $(z,b_z)$ for a finite set of such auxiliary bases, and its ceiling relative to counting times $q$-dimensional Lebesgue measure is $a_i$ on its compact support. At each attainable integer output base $p$, the auxiliary offset is unique, and its $q$-plane is exactly the affine hull of $C_p$. Restricted to the compact possible-output set, the physical measure $\mu$ is therefore precisely the auxiliary counting times Euclidean $q$-area. This gives the target ceiling $c_r$ on that set, with finite integral because the set is compact and there are finitely many output levels. Its defining maximum supplies the accepted variable-density theorem's product inequality for all allowed endpoint tuples. Apply that theorem with weights $1/2,1/2$ and continuous dimension $q$. The physical midpoint and full physical convex order are preserved by the isometric change of coordinates. For $q=0$ each nonempty sampled fiber is a point, so $S$ is finite and the weighted finite atom ceiling theorem with weights $1/2,1/2$ gives exactly the classwise estimate against counting measure. Summation over disjoint input classes gives the specified original marginals and adds their ceilings as physical measures even when the output sets overlap. For constant fiber ceilings the displayed maximum over physical pairs is bounded by its maximum over their base pairs.

Unit ceilings give $c_r=\mathbf1_{D_r}$. If the mean of two projected points lies in a supporting hyperplane $A$, their nonnegative supporting slacks average to zero, so both points belong to $A$. At an integer output base $p\in A$, the integer points in $A$ form $p+\Lambda_A$, where $\Lambda_A=\mathbb Z^n\cap\operatorname{dir}A$. Reduction modulo $2\mathbb Z^n$ on $\Lambda_A$ has kernel $2\Lambda_A$, because halving an even integer vector in the direction subspace stays there. Hence the parity image has size $2^{\operatorname{rank}\Lambda_A}$, at most $2^{n-1}$ for a supporting hyperplane. Any interior projected base has a full-dimensional continuous fiber. To see this, project an ambient interior point and, if its base differs from the given interior base, extend their segment past that base within the projection. A lift of the farther base combined strictly with the interior point gives an ambient interior point over the given base. Thus $q<d$ puts every sampled base on the projection boundary, and $n=0$ would instead force $q=d$.

For $q=d$ take $[0,2]^n\times K$ with $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ of volume one, including a singleton of counting mass one for $d=0$. Put unit density on the bases $\{0,1\}^n$ in the minus input and $\{1,2\}^n$ in the plus input. At any admissible integer midpoint the plus base is coordinatewise the complement $2-z$ of the minus base, and all mass $2^n$ reaches the one fiber over the all-ones base. That fiber has measure one. Complementary bases with identical continuous coordinates attain the constant. For $0\le q<d$ use coordinates $(z',t,u,v)\in\mathbb R^{n-1}\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^q\times\mathbb R^{d-q}$ and the full-dimensional convex body specified by $z'\in[0,2]^{n-1}$, $0\le t\le\epsilon<1$, $u\in K$ and $\|v\|_\infty\le t$, with $0<\epsilon$ and $K$ of intrinsic volume one. All sampled bases have $t=0$ and all sampled fibers have intrinsic dimension $q$. Repeat the same construction in the $n-1$ free integer coordinates. It forces total mass $2^{n-1}$ onto one unit-measure fiber and attains the bound by identical continuous coordinates.
statement:
Let $n,d\ge0$, let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, and let $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\ne\varnothing$, $q=\dim_H S$ and $\mu=\mathcal H^q|_S$ (counting measure for $q=0$). Let $\gamma_-,\gamma_+$ be finite nonnegative measures of equal mass supported on $S$, and let $\Xi_{\rm old}$ be a coupling whose midpoints belong to $S$ almost everywhere. Assume $\gamma_i\le a_i\mu$ for bounded nonnegative upper semicontinuous $a_i$ on the compact supports $E_i=\operatorname{supp}\gamma_i$. Let $E_{i,r}$ and $\gamma_{i,r}$ denote the restrictions to original base parity $r$. For $q\ge1$ put $H_q(t,s)=((t^{-1/q}+s^{-1/q})/2)^{-q}$ on positive arguments and zero if either vanishes. Put $H_0(t,s)=\min(t,s)$. Define on the physical space
$$
c_r(w)=\max_{\substack{u\in E_{-,r},\,v\in E_{+,r}\\(u+v)/2=w}} H_q(a_-(u),a_+(v)),
$$
with the empty maximum zero. Then each $c_r$ is bounded and upper semicontinuous. There is one coupling of the original marginals whose classwise midpoint laws satisfy $\rho_{{\rm old},r}\preceq_{\rm cx}\rho_r\le c_r\mu$ in full physical coordinates, and whose classwise endpoint marginals are $\gamma_{-,r},\gamma_{+,r}$. Its total midpoint law satisfies $\rho\le(\sum_r c_r)\mu$. For fiberwise constant ceilings $c_r(p,x)$ is bounded by the maximum of $H_q$ over positive class-$r$ input base pairs summing to $2p$.

In particular, for unit ceilings let $D_r=(E_{-,r}+E_{+,r})/2$. Then $\rho_r\le\mathbf1_{D_r}\mu$ and $\rho\le\kappa\mu$ with $\kappa(w)=\#\{r:w\in D_r\}\le2^n$. At a boundary base $p$ of the projection of $C$, any supporting affine hyperplane $A$ gives $\kappa(p,x)\le 2^{\operatorname{rank}(\mathbb Z^n\cap\operatorname{dir}A)}$. If $q<d$ then $n\ge1$ and $\kappa\le2^{n-1}$ on $S$. The uniform constants $2^n$ for $q=d$ and $2^{n-1}$ for $q<d$ are sharp.
title: Intrinsic parity midpoint repair under variable ceilings
